findings.description: A thread an earlier fix round already answered (and the gate deliberately left open "for the operator") now counts as open, so `pup ci wait` names `pup fix` again and `pup fix` hands the same finding back as a repeat round, each repeat climbing the model ladder.
findings.body:
**A thread a fix round already answered now comes back as a new round.**

`openThreads` now keeps every unresolved, non-outdated bot thread, whichever run opened it:

```ts
openThreads: nodesOf(threads).flatMap((thread): ReviewThread[] => {
  const [finding] = nodesOf(thread.comments);
  if (thread.isResolved !== false || typeof thread.id !== 'string') return [];
  // Only a plain `true` outdates it, so a field outside its shape stays open.
  if (thread.isOutdated === true) return [];
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/55c11b97f79c82d6af38fb9a0395ed270d4f8a4d/src/core/github.client.ts#L413-L417

That set includes threads pupitre has already replied to. `answerFixRoundThreads` replies to every relayed thread but resolves one only when the verdict is `addressed` (src/core/fix-round.service.ts:354). `threadVerdict` returns `addressed` only when the worker answered "fixed" *and* the round changed that file. Any other thread (declined, unanswered, or fixed but unverifiable) gets a reply and stays open "for the operator" (L365).

**Trigger.**
1. Round 1 relays `PRRT_x`, and the worker declines it as a false positive.
2. The round's push doesn't touch that line, so GitHub keeps `isOutdated` false.
3. The bot re-reviews the new head (the round's summary carries `REVIEW_ASK`) and sets SUCCESS "no blocking issues".

**Result.**
- `reviewDigest` (src/core/ci-wait.service.ts:277-286) prints `1 open thread(s) → pup fix <id>` instead of the merge click.
- `reviewVerdict` (src/core/fix-round.service.ts:666-674) returns the thread, so `pup fix` relays the same finding again. The kickoff carries only its first comment, so the worker has no sign it already declined it.
- `fixRoundFailure` (src/core/routing.utils.ts:221-222) counts each such round as `repeat-fix-round`, so it climbs the ladder.
- This repeats until the operator resolves the thread by hand.

**Why it's new.** Before this change, the newest-run filter dropped the thread once the bot reviewed the new head. ADR 0163 covers an earlier *bot run's* unanswered thread (#284). It doesn't cover threads pupitre itself already answered.

The rationale at routing.utils.ts:191-192 ("the review mints fresh thread ids on every head a round pushes") is now also inaccurate.

**Possible fixes.**
- Skip threads whose ids an earlier `fix_round` already relayed and answered.
- Or read whether the thread's last comment is pupitre's reply.

findings.description: `pup ci wait` treats the now-unconditional page-cap refusal as a transient failed read: on any PR with more than 100 review threads (even all resolved) it polls until the full timeout, then tells the user to re-run `pup ci wait`, which refuses again.

`ThreadSeed.earlier` is now dead (no reader or caller after this PR), while fix-round-kickoff.test.ts extends `ThreadSeed` inline with `isOutdated`; delete `earlier` and put `isOutdated?: boolean` on the shared `ThreadSeed` (general.md: "Delete old code when you replace it").

In the #284 scenario this PR targets, the digest reads `1 open thread(s), 0 important`: the important count comes from the newest status text ("no blocking issues"), though every anchored thread is an important finding.
